The titration phase must be carried out with particular caution in patients with chronic obstructive broncho-pneumopathy or another pathology (e.g. serious myasthenia) predisposing them to respiratory depression, due to the increase in the risk of respiratory depression which can cause respiratory stop. Increase in intracranial pressure, disorders of abstine consciousness should only be administered with extreme caution to patients likely to present a particular sensitivity to the brain effects of hypercapnia, such as patients with signs of intracranial hypertension, consciousness disorders, coma or brain tumors. The morphine can mask clinical evolution in patients with cranial trauma, they should only be used in this context in the event of absolute necessity. Cardiac pathology Fentanyl can cause bradycardia. It should be used with caution in patients with a history of bradyarhythmia or pre -existing bradyarhythmia. Elderly patients The data obtained following the intravenous administration of Fentanyl suggest the possibility of a reduction in its clearance and an increase in its half-life in elderly patients, who could be more sensitive to active substance than younger patients. Renal or abstine renal or hepatic insufficiency should be administered with caution in patients with liver or renal disorders, especially during the titration phase. In the event of the suspicion of serotonergic syndrome, the treatment should be stopped.

This vaccine is indicated in the prevention of invasive infections at Haemophilus influenzae type B (meningitis, septicemia, cellulite, arthritis, epiglottites, ...) in children from 2 months. This vaccine does not protect against infections due to other types of Haemophilus influenzae, nor against meningitis due to other origins. In no case can the tetanus protein contained in this vaccine replace the usual tetanical vaccination.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to active substance, one of the excipients, tetanical protein or formaldehyde (which can be present in each dose in the trace state). Known hypersensitivity appeared after an earlier injection of a conjugated Haemophilus Influenzae vaccine. Vaccination should be deferred in the event of febrile disease or acute disease.

Tocilizumab, in combination with methotrexate (MTX), is indicated for: - The treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (PR) active, severe and evolving in adult patients not previously treated by MTX. - The treatment of active Professor, moderate to severe, in adult patients who have presented either an inadequate response, or intolerance to a previous treatment with one or more background treatments (Dmards) or by one or more antagonists of the tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF). In these patients, tocilizumab can be used in monotherapy in the event of MTX intolerance, or when pursuit of MTX treatment is unsuitable. Tocilizumab has been shown, in combination with methotrexate, reduces the rate of increase in joint structural damage measured by radiography and improves functional capacities. Tocilizumab is indicated for the treatment of systemic idiopathic juvenile arthritis (AJIS) active in patients aged 1 year and more, who have presented an inadequate response to previous treatment with NSAIDs and systemic corticosteroids. Tocilizumab can be used in monotherapy (in case of MTX intolerance or when treatment with MTX is unsuitable) or in combination with MTX. Tocilizumab in combination with methotrexate (MTX) is indicated for the treatment of arthritis juvenile idiopathic polyarticular (AJIP: positive or negative rheumatoid factor and extended oligoarthritis) in patients aged 2 and over, who presented an inadequate response to a previous MTX treatment. Tocilizumab can be used in monotherapy in case of MTX intolerance, or when pursuit of MTX treatment is unsuitable. Tocilizumab is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with giant cell arteritis (ACG).

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

AMGEVITA can be used in monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate or other substantive anti -globalization agents; The association of Adalimumab with ciclosporin, azathioprine and other anti-TNF --α treatments has not been studied. In patients in whom moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis has been recently diagnosed (<3 years) and which have not been treated by methotrexate before, the effectiveness of adalimumab in combination with methotrexate has been demonstrated. Idiopathic Idiopathic Idiopathic arthritis Amgevita is indicated, in combination with methotrexate, for the treatment of active polyarticular idiopathic arthritis in adolescents from 13 years with a minimum 1.7 m2 bodily surface which did not reach a sufficient response to one or several anti -uhomatic modifiers of the disease (DMARD) to methotrexate, or are intolerant to such treatment. AMGEVITA can be used in monotherapy during methotrexate intolerance or when treatment with methotrexate is no longer possible. Adalimumab has not been studied in children under the age of 4. AMGEVITA PSORIASIC Arthritis is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis in patients responding insufficiently to treatment with substantive anti -global agents. Amgevita slows down the speed of progression of structural lesions and improves the physical functional capacities of patients with the symmetrical articular form of the disease. AMGEVITA can be used in monotherapy or in combination with substantive anti -globalization agents. Ankylosing spondylitis (Bechterew disease) Amgevita is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with active ankylosing spondylitis only responding to conventional treatments. Crohn Amgevita's disease is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Crohn's disease with average to strong pathological activity and only responding to conventional treatments, as well as for the treatment of adult patients no longer responding to infliximab or not supporting it. AMGEVITA ulcerative colitis is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis in adult patients who have not reached a sufficient response under conventional treatment, including by glucocorticoids and/or 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP) or azathioprine (AZA), or presenting intolerance or contraindication to such treatment. Psoriasis amgevita is indicated in monotherapy for the treatment of adult patients with psoriasis in moderate to severe chronic plates and candidates for systemic treatment or puvatherapy. Suppurated hidradenitis (Verneuil disease) Amgevita is indicated for the treatment of moderate active forms with severe Hidradenitis Suppurée (Verneuil disease) in adult patients who did not respond satisfactorily to systemic antibiotic therapy. Uveitis amgevita is indicated for induction (in combination with corticosteroids) and the maintenance of a remission in adult patients with non -infectious intermediate, posterior or papuvitic in the event of dependence on corticosteroids, not satisfactorizing corticosteroids with or without immunomodulators or Corticosteroids. The association with corticosteroids and/or immunomodulators depends on anatomical and functional evolution.

This medication is indicated to reduce high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults. Indapamide is a diuretic. Most diuretics increase the amount of urine produced by the kidneys. However, indapamide is different from other diuretics because it only has a slight increase in the amount of urine produced. In addition, Indapamide dilates blood vessels, which allows blood to circulate more easily. This helps reduce blood pressure.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Augmentin is indicated for the treatment of the following infections in adults and children: - acute bacterial sinusitis (diagnosed appropriately), - acute average otitis, - acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis (diagnosed appropriately), - acute community pneumonia, - cystitis, - pyelonephritis, - infections of the skin and soft tissue, in particular Cellulite, animal bites, severe dental abscesses with cellulite propagation, - bone and joint infections, in particular osteomyelitis. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials.

Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.

Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

ENTécavir is indicated in the treatment of adult patients with chronic infection by the hepatitis B virus (VHB) presenting • a compensated liver disease with the demonstration of active viral replication and with at least one of the following criteria: o Persistent elevation of serum rates of Alanine Aminatransferase (ALAT). o Active inflammation and/or histologically proven fibrosis. • decompensated liver disease. Uses: Anemia in the event of chronic renal failure anemia chronic symptomatic anemia requiring transfusions, secondary to chronic renal failure of advanced stage (pre-dialyzed and dialysis patients). Operating preparation to avoid homologous blood transfusions stimulation of erythropoiesis before significant orthopedic intervention in order to reduce homologous blood transfusions and to correct postoperative anemia in adults without iron deficiency. Binocrit treatment should be reserved for patients with moderate anemia (HB 10–13 g/DL) and a blood loss provided from 900 to 1800 ml. Operating preparation with autologous donation program Stimulation of erythropoiesis in order to increase autologous blood donations and limit the fall of hemoglobin in patient adults for major elective surgical interventions, which are not able to provide the required autologous blood units. Treatment with binocrit should only be introduced in patients without iron deficiency and suffering from moderate anemia (HB 10–13 g/dl) when measures increasing autologous blood donations are not applicable or insufficient and the planned surgical intervention requires a large blood volume (4 or more units in women; 5 or more units). Examples of use: reduced values ​​of hemoglobin, need for autologous blood ≥5 units, short operating preparation time.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Caution will therefore be of rigor in the treatment of patients with a high risk of gastrointestinal complications under NSAIDs: for example elderly patients, people treated simultaneously with other NSAIDs, with inhibitors of platelet aggregation (such as acetylsalicylic acid) or with glucocorticoids or patients drinking alcohol or antecedent Gastrointestinal pathologies such as ulcers or hemorrhages. Oral anticoagulants include coumarin type warfarin and new oral anticoagulants (eg apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban). In patients treated jointly with warfarin or similar active substances, some have been observed severe hemorrhages, some of which have been fatal. Due to the increase in thromboplastin time (INR) reported, coagulation/INR should be monitored in patients with coumarin type warfarin, at the start of treatment or after a modification of the celebrity dose (see under "interactions"). Systemic idiopathic idiopathic arthritis, including Cellcoxib, should be used with caution in the systemic form of AJI because of the risk of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Patients with systemic AIJ, receiving celebration, should be monitored in order to detect any development of coagulation test anomalies.

Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

According to the indications and the germs in question, the antibiotic has the best benefit / risk ratio should be used as a first intention. They are limited to adult infections due to sensitive germs. Especially - curative treatment: jirovecii pneumocystis infections; Uro-genital infections of man, especially prostatitis. Prevention of Jirovecii pneumocystis infections, in immunocompromised, and especially in patients infected with HIV and at risk of pneumocystosis. In these cases, the incidence of cerebral toxoplasmosis also seems to be decreased in the studies conducted in patients who receive the association Trimethethoprime-Sulfamethoxazole and tolerate it for long periods; In the event of a bone moelle transplant or organ transplantation. On the other hand, taking into account the benefit/risk ratio compared to other products, epidemiology and bacterial resistance observed in these pathologies: treatment: - high and low urinary tract infections; In particular monodose treatment of uncomplicated acute cystitis of women under 65; - otitis and sinusitis, but only after bacteriological documentation; - certain bronchopulmonary infections; - Digestive infections, and typhoid fever. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials.

Infectious - tuberculosis pericarditis and serious forms of tuberculosis bringing the vital prognosis into play; - Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia with severe hypoxia. Ophthalmological - anterior and severe posterior uveitis; - edematous exophthalmias; - Some optical neuropathies, in relay of intravenous corticosteroid therapy (in this indication, the first -line oral route is not recommended). ENT - certain serous otitis; - Nasosinusian polyposis; - certain acute or chronic sinusitis; - Seasonal allergic rhinitis in short cure; - Stidly acute laryngitis (sub-glottical laryngitis) in children. Respiratory - persistent asthma preferably in short cure in the event of failure of the treatment by way inhaled to high doses; - Asthma exacerbations, in particular serious acute asthma; - chronic obstructive chronic bronchopneumopathy in evaluation of the reversibility of obstructive syndrome; - evolutionary sarcoidosis; - diffuse interstitial pulmonary fibrosis. Rheumatological - rheumatoid arthritis and certain polyarthritis; - Rhizomelic polyarthritis pseudo and Horton's disease; - Fet joint rheumatism; - Severe and rebellious cervico-brachial neuralgia. Transplantation of organs and allogenic hematopoietic stem cells - Prophylaxis or treatment of transplant rejection; - Prophylaxis or treatment of the reaction of the graft against the host.

Depakine is mainly indicated, preferably in monotherapy, in generalized primary epilepsies: Petit-Mal/Absences, Massive bilateral myoclonies, Grand-Mal with or without myoclonies, photosensitive forms. Depakine is also effective, alone or in combination with other antiepileptics in the following indications: secondary generalized epilepsies, including West syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Partial epilepsies with elementary symptomatology or complex symptomatology (psychosensory forms, psychomotor forms). Secondarily generalized epilepsies. Mixed forms (generalized and partial). Furthermore, Depakine, an injectable preparation can be used in the context of well -defined therapeutic plans in adults: as a second -intention product in the face of generalized convulsive crises ("great badly status") when initial treatment with benzodiazepines (first -line treatment) did not allow to put an end to crises; As a first -line product during generalized non -convulsive crises (status of absence) as treatment that can replace that based on benzodiazepines; As a second -intention product in the face of convulsive and non -convulsive crises (simple or complex focal crises) when initial treatment with benzodiazepines (first -line treatment) has not made it possible to put an end to crises.

Use in the treatment of onychomycosis is not clinically documented. Candidemia. Méningoée cryptococcosis and prophylaxis of recurrences of this disease in side patients. In some patients with meningeal cryptococcosis, the antifungal effect of fluconazole develops more slowly than that of amphotericin B or the association of amphotericin B and flucytosin, but there is however no significant difference from the healing rate. Fluconazole can also be used to treat other cryptococcosis (for example pulmonary or skin). Patients without associated diseases, side patients, transplanted and other immunosupprima patients can also be treated by fluconazole. Fluconazole should not be used for the treatment of ringworm (tinea capitis) in children and adolescents.
Contraindications: Fluconazole should not be administered: • in the event of hypersensitivity to active substance, other Azole derivatives or one of the excipients. • In children under the age of 6, due to the pharmaceutical form. Coadministration with terfenadine is contraindicated in patients treated with fluconazole with repeated doses greater than or equal to 400 mg per day on the basis of the results of a repeated dose interaction study. Coadministration with other drugs known to prolong the QT interval and metabolized by cytochromes P450 (CYP) 3A4 such as Cisapride, Astemizole, Pimozide, Quinidine and Erythromycin is contraindicated in patients treated with fluconazole. Esophagitis by gastroesophageal reflux of low to moderate intensity: in the treatment of esophagitis by gastroesophageal reflux of low to moderate intensity, the recommended dose is 40 mg of Famotidine twice a day (or two film-coated tablets dosed at 40 mg in Famotidine). Famotidine must be administered at the end of dialysis or after the session, because part of the active substance is eliminated by dialysis.

Doctaxel is indicated in monotherapy in the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of cytotoxic chemotherapy, having included anthracycline or an alkylant agent. Doctaxel in combination with trastuzumab is indicated in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer with tumor exhaustion of Her2, in patients not pre-pri-pre-priest by chemotherapy for their metastatic disease. Doctaxel in combination with capecitabine is indicated in the treatment of locally advanced breast cancer or metastatic after failure of cytotoxic chemotherapy that included anthracycline. Lung cancer non -small Doctaxel cells is indicated in the treatment of non -small cells bronchial cancer locally advanced or metastatic, after failure of anterior chemotherapy. Doctaxel in combination with CISPLATINE is indicated in the treatment of non -resusable, locally advanced or metastatic bronchial cancer, in patients who have not received anterior chemotherapy in this indication. DOCETAXEL prostate cancer in association with prednisone or prednisolone is indicated in the treatment of cancer of the metastatic prostate resistant to castration. Doctaxel in combination with antiandrogenic treatment (ADT), with or without prednisone or prednisolone, is indicated in the treatment of cancer of the hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate. Doctrical cancer doctaxel, in combination with cisplatin and 5-flooding is indicated in the treatment of metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma, including the adenocarcinoma of the esogastric junction, in patients not pre-prone to chemotherapy for their metastatic disease. Cancer of the upper aero-digestive tracks Doetaxel in association with cisplatin and 5-florouracile is indicated in the induction treatment of locally advanced epidermoid carcinomas of the upper aero-digestive tracks.

Dornat Plus® is a unique combination of several phytoactive extracts and supplements that act mainly against stress and insomnia disorders by their relaxing and sedative properties. Due to their synergy, the effects of each of its components are amplified in order to improve the quality of sleep and treat the various physio-spathological disorders linked to chronic insomnia. Anemia in the event of chronic renal failure anemia chronic symptomatic anemia requiring transfusions, secondary to chronic renal failure of advanced stage (pre-dialyzed and dialysis patients). Cancer patients Treatment of symptomatic anemia and reduction in transfusions in adult cancer patients with hemoglobin levels less than 10.5 g/dl and expected for chemotherapy for a minimum of 2 months. In clinical trials, in case of chemotherapy not containing platinum, treatment with EPREX has generally been introduced after 2 to 3 cycles of chemotherapy. Operating preparation to avoid homologous blood transfusions stimulation of erythropoiesis before significant orthopedic intervention in order to reduce homologous blood transfusions and to correct postoperative anemia in adults without iron deficiency. Treatment with EPREX should be reserved for patients with moderate anemia (HB 10–13 g/DL) and a blood loss provided from 900 to 1800 ml. Operating preparation with autologous donation program Stimulation of erythropoiesis in order to increase autologous blood donations and limit the fall of hemoglobin in patients forebod for major elective surgical interventions, which are not able to provide the required autologous blood units. Treatment with EPREX should only be introduced in patients without iron deficiency and suffering from moderate anemia (HB 10–13 g/dl) when measures increasing autologous blood donations are not applicable or insufficient and the planned surgical intervention requires significant blood volume (4 or more units in women; 5 or more units). Examples of use: reduced values ​​of hemoglobin, need for autologous blood ≥5 units, short operating preparation time.

Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

Treatment of premature ejaculation (EP) in adult men aged 18 to 64. Dapoxetine must only be prescribed to patients bringing together all the following criteria: · Time of intravaginal ejaculation (IELT) less than two minutes; and ejaculation which, permanently or recurrently, occurs with minimal sexual stimulation, before, during or shortly after penetration and before the patient wishes; and significant personal suffering or interpersonal difficulties as a consequence of the EP; and · Bad ejaculation control; and history of premature ejaculation in the majority of sex in the last 6 months. Dapoxetine should only be administered as a treatment treatment before planned sexual activity. Dapoxetine should not be prescribed to delay ejaculation in men who have not been diagnosed with an EP.
TherapeuticClass: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (ISRS) during premature ejaculation

Uses: Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Ofloxacin 200 mg, scored film-coated tablet is indicated in the treatment of following bacterial infections. Particular attention should be paid to information available on bacterial resistance to OFLOXACINE before initiating the treatment. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials. In adults - acute pyelonephritis and complicated infections of urinary tract. - Prostatitis of bacterial origin, orchi-epididymitis. - Pelvic inflammatory pathology, in combination with other antibiotics. For the infections mentioned below, ofloxacin should be used only when the antibiotics usually recommended for the treatment of these infections, are deemed inappropriate): - uncomplicated acute cystitis. - Uretrite. - osteoarticular infections. - complicated infections of skin and soft tissue. - Aigue sinusitis of bacterial origin. - Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive broncho-pneumopathy, including chronic bronchitis. - Community pneumonia. Special situations inhalation of anthrax (coal): prophylaxis after exposure and curative treatment during the treatment of infections at pseudomonas aeruginosa and staphylococcus aureus, the emergence of resistant mutants has been described and can justify the association of another antibiotic. Microbiological monitoring in search of such resistance must be considered in particular in the event of suspicion of failure. The use of OFLOXACINE in serious infections, in particular bacteremic at pseudomonas aeruginosa and acinetobacter, is not recommended.

For the infections mentioned below, OFLOXACINE should only be used when the antibiotics recommended in the initial treatments of these infections are deemed inappropriate: complicated infections of soft and skin. Osteo-articular infections. Acute cystitis, infections of the exacerbation urethra of chronic and recurrent bronchitis caused by the Haemophilus influenzae or other gram negative and multi-resistant germs as well as by the staphylococcus gold. The use of Ofloxacin is indicated in the event of pneumonia due to so -called problems (e.g. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Legionella, Staphylococcus). In the outpatient sector, pneumonia is often due to pneumococci that are not very sensitive to OFLOXACINE. Infections of the small basin (Pelvis) in association with other treatments. Anti-infectious prophylaxis in patients with deficient immune defenses (eg in neutropenic phase). Please consult the official recommendations for the appropriate employment of antibiotics, in particular recommendations to reduce the increase in antibiotic resistance. Children and adolescents The use of OFLOXACINE is not indicated in children and adolescents under the age of 18.

Enoxaparin is indicated in adults in: - Prophylactic treatment of venous thromboembolic disease in moderate and high risk surgery, in particular in orthopedic or general surgery, including oncological surgery. - Prophylactic treatment of venous thromboembolic disease in patients with acute medical condition (such as acute heart insufficiency, respiratory failure, severe infections or rheumatic diseases) and whose mobility is reduced, at risk of increased venous thromboembolic. - The treatment of deep venous thrombosis (TVP) and pulmonary embolism (EP), to the exclusion of EP capable of undergoing thrombolytic or surgical treatment. - The prevention of the formation of a thrombus in the extracorporeal circuit circuit during hemodialysis. - Acute coronary syndrome: * Treatment of unstable angina and myocardial infarction without elevation of the ST segment (Nstemi), administered in combination with oral acetylsalicylic acid. * Treatment of acute myocardial infarction with elevation of the ST (STEMI) segment, including patients eligible for medical treatment or percutaneous coronary intervention (ICP).
Packaging: Box of 2 1 ml syringes (should not be administered intramuscularly.)

In some patients with meningeal cryptococcosis, the antifungal effect of fluconazole develops more slowly than that of amphotericin B or the association of amphotericin B and flucytosin, but there is however no significant difference from the healing rate. Gadovist is indicated in adults and children of all ages (including the newborn baby) for: · enhancement of the contrast in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the cranial and spinal territories. · Enhancement of the contrast in MRI of the liver or kidneys in patients with a strong suspicion or an obvious presence of focused lesions, in order to classify these lesions as benign or malignant. · Raise of contrast in magnetic resonance angiography (ARM). Uses: Children: Growth delay linked to a somatotropic deficit. Growth delay in girls with gonadic dysgenesis (Turner syndrome). Growth delay in prepuberal children due to chronic kidney failure. Growth delay (current size <-2.5 DS and adjusted parental size <-1 DS) in children born small for gestational age (PTAG) with a weight and/or birth size below -2 DS, not having caught up their growth delay (growth speed <0 DS in the past year) at the age of 4 or more. Growth delay linked to Noonan syndrome. Adults: Somatotropic deficit acquired in childhood: once their growth is completed, the secretory capacity in growth hormone should be reassessed in patients with a somatotropic deficit acquired in childhood. No tests are required in patients with more than three pituitary hormonal deficits, in patients with severe somatotropic deficit due to a defined genetic cause, due to hypothalamo-pituitary structural anomalies, due to tumors of the central nervous system or due to an intra-cranial irradiation in high doses, or in patients with somatotrope deficit Secondary on a pathology or hypothalamo-pituitary involvement, if the Dosage of IGF-1 (Insulin-Like Growth Factor 1) is <-2 DS at least four weeks after stopping treatment by growth hormone. In all other patients, IGF-1 dosage and a dynamic growth hormone stimulation test are required. Somatotropic deficit acquired in adulthood: significant somatotropic deficit in the context of a known hypothalamo-hypophyseal pathology, an intra-cranial irradiation or a traumatic brain lesion. The somatotropic deficit must be associated with another deficit axis, other than prolactin. The somatotropic deficit will have to be highlighted during a dynamic test after establishing an adequate hormonal substitution of any other hormonal deficit. In adults, insulin hypoglycemia is the dynamic test of choice. When insulin hypoglycemia is contraindicated, alternative dynamic tests should be used. The Arginine-GHRH combination is recommended. Arginine or glucagon test can also be envisaged; However, the diagnostic value of these tests is less well established than that of the test of insulin hypoglycemia.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. Glivec is indicated in the treatment: • Adult and children with chronic myeloid leukemia (LMC) PHIDALPHIE (BCR-abl) chromosome (BCR-ABL) newly diagnosed when bone marrow transplant cannot be considered as first-line treatment. • Adult and children with LMC PH+ in chronic phase after failure of treatment with alpha interferon, or in the accelerated phase or in a blastic crisis. • Adult patients and children with acute lymphoid leukemia chromosome positive philadelphia (LAL PH+) newly diagnosed in combination with chemotherapy. • Adult patients with LAL PH+ refractory or relapse in monotherapy. • Adult patients with myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative syndromes (SMD/SMP) associated with rearrangements of the CEO gene (Platelet-Derived Growth Factor Receptor). • Adult patients with hypereosinophilic syndrome (SHE) at an advanced stage and/or chronic leukemia with eosinophiles (LCE) associated with a rearrangement of FIP1L1- CEO. Glvec's effect on the outcome of a bone marrow transplant was not evaluated. 3 Glivec is indicated in • The treatment of adult patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST - Gastrintestinal Stromal Tumours) Malignant Kit (CD 117) Positive non -rescinable and/or metastatic. • Addressing treatment of adult patients with a significant risk of relapse after resection of a positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor (CD117). Patients with a low or very low risk should not be treated. • Treatment of adult patients with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP or Darier-Ferrand disease) unwanted and adult patients with dfsp in relapse and/or metastatic not falling under surgical treatment. In adults and pediatric patients, Glivec the efficiency is based on global hematogic and cytogenetic responses and progression -free survival in LMC, on the levels of hematological and cytogenetic responses of LAL PH+, SMD/SMP, on the levels of hematological responses of Shen/LCE and on GIST. Bettleable and/or metastatic and DFSP and survival without relapse in the adjuvant treatment of GISTs. The experience with Glivec in patients with SMD/SMP associated with rearrangements of the CEO gene is very limited. With the exception of the LMC in the newly diagnosed chronic phase, there is no controlled clinical study demonstrating a clinical benefit or an extension of the lifespan, for these diseases.

This medication is indicated to reduce high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults. Indapamide is a diuretic. Most diuretics increase the amount of urine produced by the kidneys. However, indapamide is different from other diuretics because it only has a slight increase in the amount of urine produced. In addition, Indapamide dilates blood vessels, which allows blood to circulate more easily. This helps reduce blood pressure.

In women A treatment with Gonal-F Monitoring of the trigger for ovulation by an injection of human chorionic gonadotrophin (HCG) is indicated to stimulate follicular growth and ovulation in women with a hypothalamo-pituitary dysfunction which have oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea. These women are classified in group II of WHO. They usually receive clomiphene citrate as a primary treatment. They present an endogenous estrogen production and therefore have their rules either spontaneously or after the administration of progestins. Many of these patients have polycystic ovary syndrome (SOPK). This syndrome is classified in group II of WHO. Gonal-F is indicated to stimulate multiple follicular growth in women who use medically assisted procreation techniques such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), the intratubal transfer of gametes and the intratubal transfer of embryos. Gonal-F, in combination with a luteeinizing hormone preparation (LH), is used to stimulate follicular maturation in women with serious LH and FSH deficit. In clinical trials, these patients were defined by a serum endogenous LH rate <1.2 IU/L. In humans Gonal-F is used in combination with human choriogonadotropin to stimulate spermatogenesis in men suffering from congenital or acquired hypogonadodotic hypogonadism.

The treatment should be administered exclusively in patients with moderate anemia (interval of hemoglobin concentrations [HB] between 10 and 13 g/dl [between 6.2 and 8.1 mmol/L], without iron deficiency), if blood savings procedures are not available or not sufficient when the major non -urgent intervention required requires a significant volume of blood (4 or more or more units in humans). The use must be reserved for patients with moderate anemia (for example, interval of hemoglobin concentrations between 10 and 13 g/dl or between 6.2 and 8.1 mmol/l) which do not have access to a delayed autologous sample program and in which we expect moderate blood loss (900 to 1,800 ml). Uses: Treatment of adult patients suffering from the following infections: • Nosocomial pneumonia, provided that it is proven or very likely that it is caused by stumps of staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pneumoniae sensitive to linezolid. Experience in infections caused by pneumococci resistant to penicillin is limited. The linezolid is not effective in the event of Gram -negative infections. If a mixed infection due to gram negative germs is suspected or attested, a specific treatment must be established simultaneously against gram negative germs. To date, only Aztréonam and the Aminosides have been tested. • Complicated infections of skin and soft tissues: with regard to the treatment of complicated infections of the skin and soft tissues, linezolid is indicated only when it is established, after determining microbiological sensitivity, that infection is caused by sensitive gram -related bacteria belonging to staphylococcus aureus, stuptococcus pyogenic or Agalactiae. The linezolid is not effective in the event of Gram -negative infections. In patients suffering from complicated infections of the skin and soft tissues, in whom a co-infection due to gram negative germs is presumed or attested, the linezolid should be used only if there is no other possible treatment (see the section "Warnings and precautions"). In such cases, you must simultaneously establish a treatment for gram negative germs. To date, only Aztréonam and the Aminosides have been tested. There is no experience in the treatment of diabetic ulcers or decubitus. • Enterococcus faecium infections resistant to vancomycin, including bacteremia. There is no experience in the treatment of SNC infections, osteomyelitis and endocarditis. Official recommendations for the appropriate use of antibiotics must be followed, in particular the recommendations for use intended to prevent the proliferation of antibiotic resistance. It is therefore recommended to make the diagnosis and start treatment with the linezolid in a hospital environment, under the control of a specialist, for example an infectiologist. The treatment can be prosecuted ambulatically.

Form: Solution to be diluted for infusion
Uses: The active substance contained is the zolédronic acid which belongs to a group of substances called bisphosphonates. Zoledronic acid acts by focusing on the bone and slowing down the bone renewal rate. It is used: - to prevent bone complications, ex. Fractures, in adult patients with bone metastases (dissemination of main site cancer); - to reduce the calcium level in the blood of adult patients when it is high due to the presence of a tumor. Tumors can accelerate the usual bone renewal so that the amount of calcium released by the bone is increased. This pathology is called hypercalcemia induced by tumors.

Imatinib is indicated in the treatment: • Adult patients and children with chronic myeloid leukemia (LMC) PHIDALPHIE (BCR-ABL) POSITIVE (PH+) newly diagnosed when the bone marrow transplant cannot be considered as a first-line treatment. • Adult and children with LMC PH+ in chronic phase after failure of treatment with alpha interferon, or in the accelerated phase or in a blastic crisis. • Adult patients and children with acute lymphoid leukemia chromosome positive philadelphia (LAL PH+) newly diagnosed in combination with chemotherapy. • Adult patients with LAL PH+ refractory or relapse in monotherapy. • Adult patients with myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative syndromes (SMD/SMP) associated with rearrangements of the CEO gene (Platelet-Derived Growth Factor Receptor). • Adult patients with hypereosinophilic syndrome (SHE) at an advanced stage and/or chronic leukemia with eosinophiles (LCE) associated with a rearrangement of FIP1L1- CEO. The effect of imatinib on the outcome of a bone marrow transplant was not evaluated. Imatinib is indicated in • The treatment of adult patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST - Gastrintestinal Stromal Tumours) Malignant Kit (CD 117) positive and/or metastatic positive. • Addressing treatment of adult patients with a significant risk of relapse after resection of a positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor (CD117). Patients with a low or very low risk should not be treated. • Treatment of adult patients with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP or Darier-Ferrand disease) unwanted and adult patients with dfsp in relapse and/or metastatic not falling under surgical treatment. In adults and pediatric patients, the efficiency of imatinib is based on overall hematological and cytogenetic responses and progression -free survival in the LMC, the levels of hematological and cytogenetic responses of LAL PH+, SMD/SMP, on the levels of hematological responses of Shen/LCE and on the rates of objective patients in GIST Bettleable and/or metastatic and DFSP and survival without relapse in the adjuvant treatment of GISTs. Experience with imatinib in patients with SMD/SMP associated with rearrangements of the PDGFR gene is very limited. With the exception of the LMC in the newly diagnosed chronic phase, there is no controlled clinical study demonstrating a clinical benefit or an extension of the lifespan, for these diseases.

Oral anticoagulants include coumarin type warfarin and new oral anticoagulants (eg apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban). In patients treated jointly with warfarin or similar active substances, some have been observed severe hemorrhages, some of which have been fatal. Due to the increase in thromboplastin time (INR) reported, coagulation/INR should be monitored in patients with coumarin type warfarin, at the start of treatment or after a modification of the celebrity dose (see under "interactions"). Celebrex 100 mg and 200 mg capsules contain lactose (142.2 mg respectively 47.3 mg, calculated in the form of anhydrous substance). This medication should not be used by people with rare metabolic disease such as galactose intolerance, lapp-lactase deficit or glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome. Systemic idiopathic idiopathic arthritis, including Cellcoxib, should be used with caution in the systemic form of AJI because of the risk of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Patients with systemic AIJ, receiving celebration, should be monitored in order to detect any development of coagulation test anomalies.

Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

Form: Solution for IM / IV injection at 500 mg
Uses: Amikacin 250 mg, powder for injection solution is indicated in adults and children in curative treatment of severe infections due to identified or suspected bacterial species, microbiologically sensitive to amikacin. Under these conditions, Amikacin 250 mg powder for injection solution can be used: - in the following infections :. Urinary infections ,. Endocarditis ,. meningitis ,. osteo-articular infections ,. listeriosis ,. skin and soft tissue infections. Patients that can present an associated or suspected bacteremia of being associated with one of the infections mentioned above, - in particular in risk situations (septic shocks not documented microbiologically, late nosocomial infections, infections on foreign body), - especially in subjects at risk (patients with cystic fibrosis, immunode -depressed, newborns). Amikacin is generally used in combination with other antibiotics, especially with beta-lactams. However, it can be prescribed in monotherapy in certain clinical situations, notably in the treatment of urinary tract infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials.

Clinical indications when the pathogen is included in the antimicrobial activity spectrum of doxycycline. PNEUMONIE respiratory tract infections: Lobary pneumonia and bronchopneumonia due to germs sensitive to doxycycline. Other infections of the ENT sphere and the pharyngitis, amygdalite, medium otitis, bronchitis and sinusitis respiratory tract. Penicillin is the first-line antibiotic for the treatment of upper respiratory tract infections caused by group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus, as well as for the prevention of fever joint rheumatism. Urinary tract infections and genitalia pyelonephritis, cystitis, uretritis and non -specific uretritis (non -gonococcal urethritis, venereal lymphogranulomatosis). Doxycycline is indicated during gonocococcal infections as an extra treatment during a suspected or proven co-infection in Chlamydia trachomatis. Doxycycline gastrointestinal infections is indicated for the treatment and selective prevention of cholera. Infections of the skin and soft tissues, furunculosis, phlegmon, abscesses, traumatic or post-operative infected wounds, paronychia. When processing soft tissue infections by doxycycline, the necessary surgical measures should be taken simultaneously. OPHTALMIC Infections The doxycycline is indicated during trachoma, even if - as the examination by immunofluorescence reveals - the pathogenic germ cannot always be eliminated. Condjunctivitis with inclusions (pool conjunctivitis) can be treated by doxycycline alone or in combination with topical drugs. Borreliosis, Lyme disease Lyme disease in stage I and II, either during skin manifestations with temporary articular manifestations and temporary or limited neurological manifestations. Recurrent epidemic fever with lice and exanthematic typhus The doxycycline is indicated in the treatment of recurrent epidemic fever with lice (due to Borrelia revers) and that of the exanthematical typhus (due to Rickettsia prowazekii). Leptospirosis Doxycycline is indicated for the prevention and treatment of leptospirosis. Other infections ornithose, prostatitis, inguinal granuloma (due to carymmatobacterium granulomatis), syphilis, franboesia (pian), soft chancre and angina of plaut-vincent. Malaria due to plasmodium falciparum resistant to chloroquine. During acute intestinal amibiase, doxycycline is indicated can be useful in addition to amoebicides. Prophylaxis When the risk of infection is high, doxycycline is indicated in the prevention of the typhus of brush (due to Rickettsia tsutsuga mushi "scrub typhus"), diarrhea of ​​travelers (enterotoxic strains of E. coli) and leptospirosis, as well as malaria in regions where plagues Falciparum are resistant to chloroquine. The official recommendations for a measured use of antibiotics must be respected, in particular the recommendations for use intended to prevent the proliferation of resistance to antibiotics.

Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

No benefit in survival or other clinically significant effects of treatment have been demonstrated in patients whose expression of the epidermal growth factor (EGFR) of the tumor (determined by IHC) was negative. Pancreas cancer: Erlotinib, in combination with gemcitabine, is indicated in the treatment of metastatic pancreatic cancer. Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Neupogen is indicated in reducing the duration of neutropenia and the incidence of feverish neutropenia in patients treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy for malignant pathology (with the exception of chronic myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes), and in reducing the duration of neutropenia in patients Myelosuppressive followed by marrow transplant and an increased risk of prolonged severe neutropenia. Neupogen’s safety and efficiency are similar in adults and children receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy. Neupogen is indicated in the mobilization of progenitor stem cells (CSP) in the circulating blood. The long -term administration of Neupogen is indicated in patients, children or adults, with severe congenital, cyclical or idiopathic neutropenia with a level of neutrophilic polynuclear ≤ 0.5 x 109/L and history of severe or recurring infections, in order to increase the level of neutrophils and reduce the incidence and the duration of the episodes infectious. Filgrastim is indicated in reducing the duration of neutropenia and the incidence of febrile neutropenia in patients treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy for malignant pathology (with the exception of chronic myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes), and in reducing the duration of neutropenia in patients Myelosuppressive therapy followed by a bone marrow transplant and with increased risk of prolonged severe neutropenia. Filgrastim's tolerance and efficiency are similar in adults and children receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy. The filgrastim is indicated in the mobilization of progenitor stem cells (CSP) in the circulating blood. The long -term administration of Filgrastim is indicated to increase the level of neutrophils and reduce the incidence and duration of infectious episodes in patients, children or adults, with severe congenital, cyclic or idiopathic neutropenia with an absolute number of neutrophilic (PNN) polynuclear (PNN) ≤ 0.5 x 109 /L and history of severe or recurring infections. Filgrastim is indicated in the treatment of persistent neutropenia (PNN ≤ 1.0 x 109 /l) in patients infected with HIV at an advanced stage, in order to reduce the risk of bacterial infection when other options intended to correct neutropenia are inadequate.
Packaging: Box of 5 pre-filled syringes of 0.5 ml

Uses: Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

• schizophrenia. • Olanzapine is indicated in monotherapy, or in treatment associated with lithium or valproate, for the treatment of acute manic episodes of bipolar disorders. Adults Ofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of bacterial infections with germs sensitive to OFLOXACINE. The mode of administration (intravenous or orally) depends on the indication and severity of the infection: pyelonephritis. Prostatitis, epididymitis, orchitis sepsis due to urogenital infections. Ofloxacin is not indicated in the treatment of syphilis and trichomonases. For the infections mentioned below, OFLOXACINE should only be used when the antibiotics recommended in the initial treatments of these infections are deemed inappropriate: complicated infections of soft and skin. Osteo-articular infections. Acute cystitis, infections of the exacerbation urethra of chronic and recurrent bronchitis caused by the Haemophilus influenzae or other gram negative and multi-resistant germs as well as by the staphylococcus gold. The use of Ofloxacin is indicated in the event of pneumonia due to so -called problems (e.g. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Legionella, Staphylococcus). In the outpatient sector, pneumonia is often due to pneumococci that are not very sensitive to OFLOXACINE. Infections of the small basin (Pelvis) in association with other treatments. Anti-infectious prophylaxis in patients with deficient immune defenses (eg in neutropenic phase). Please consult the official recommendations for the appropriate employment of antibiotics, in particular recommendations to reduce the increase in antibiotic resistance. Children and adolescents The use of OFLOXACINE is not indicated in children and adolescents under the age of 18.
