Ofloxacin 200 mg, scored film-coated tablet is indicated in the treatment of following bacterial infections. Particular attention should be paid to information available on bacterial resistance to OFLOXACINE before initiating the treatment. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials. In adults - acute pyelonephritis and complicated infections of urinary tract. - Prostatitis of bacterial origin, orchi-epididymitis. - Pelvic inflammatory pathology, in combination with other antibiotics. For the infections mentioned below, ofloxacin should be used only when the antibiotics usually recommended for the treatment of these infections, are deemed inappropriate): - uncomplicated acute cystitis. - Uretrite. - osteoarticular infections. - complicated infections of skin and soft tissue. - Aigue sinusitis of bacterial origin. - Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive broncho-pneumopathy, including chronic bronchitis. - Community pneumonia. Special situations inhalation of anthrax (coal): prophylaxis after exposure and curative treatment during the treatment of infections at pseudomonas aeruginosa and staphylococcus aureus, the emergence of resistant mutants has been described and can justify the association of another antibiotic. Microbiological monitoring in search of such resistance must be considered in particular in the event of suspicion of failure. The use of OFLOXACINE in serious infections, in particular bacteremic at pseudomonas aeruginosa and acinetobacter, is not recommended.

Adults Ofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of bacterial infections with germs sensitive to OFLOXACINE. The mode of administration (intravenous or orally) depends on the indication and severity of the infection: pyelonephritis. Prostatitis, epididymitis, orchitis sepsis due to urogenital infections. Ofloxacin is not indicated in the treatment of syphilis and trichomonases. For the infections mentioned below, OFLOXACINE should only be used when the antibiotics recommended in the initial treatments of these infections are deemed inappropriate: complicated infections of soft and skin. Osteo-articular infections. Acute cystitis, infections of the exacerbation urethra of chronic and recurrent bronchitis caused by the Haemophilus influenzae or other gram negative and multi-resistant germs as well as by the staphylococcus gold. The use of Ofloxacin is indicated in the event of pneumonia due to so -called problems (e.g. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Legionella, Staphylococcus). In the outpatient sector, pneumonia is often due to pneumococci that are not very sensitive to OFLOXACINE. Infections of the small basin (Pelvis) in association with other treatments. Anti-infectious prophylaxis in patients with deficient immune defenses (eg in neutropenic phase). Please consult the official recommendations for the appropriate employment of antibiotics, in particular recommendations to reduce the increase in antibiotic resistance. Children and adolescents The use of OFLOXACINE is not indicated in children and adolescents under the age of 18.

• schizophrenia. • Olanzapine is indicated in monotherapy, or in treatment associated with lithium or valproate, for the treatment of acute manic episodes of bipolar disorders. No other therapeutic association has been approved for the treatment of acute manic episodes linked to bipolar disorders. • When, in patients with bipolar disorders, an acute manic episode responds to olanzapine, olanzapine is indicated for the prophylaxis of recurrences. Due to insufficient data concerning possible late complications in this patient population, prophylactic treatment should be limited to 12 months after the correct initial response. If the doctor decides to extend the use beyond 12 months, it is then necessary to proceed at periodic intervals close to the assessment of the benefit/risk ratio of the drug for each of the patients taken individually.

Omeprazole is used to treat the following conditions: in adults: - gastroesophageal reflux (GERD). The acid of the stomach dates back to the esophagus (the tube that connects the throat to the stomach) causing pain, inflammation and burns. - Ulcers in the upper part of your intestine (duodenal ulcer) or your stomach (gastric ulcer). - Ulcers infected with a bacteria called Helicobacter pylori. In this case, your doctor can also prescribe antibiotics that make it possible to treat infection and cure ulcer. - Stomach ulcers associated with taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Omeprazole can also be used for prevention of these if you take NSAIDs. - An excess of acid in the stomach due to a size in the pancreas (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome) in children: children over one year old and with a body weight ≥ 10 kg- Gastro-œsophageal reflux (GERD). The acid of the stomach dates back to the esophagus (the tube that connects the throat to the stomach) causing pain, inflammation and burns. - Symptoms in children may include lifts into the mouth of the contents of the stomach (regurgitation), vomiting and limited weight gain. Children over 4 years old and adolescents with ulcers infected with a bacteria called Helicobacter pylori. In this case, the doctor can also prescribe antibiotics to your child which make it possible to treat the infection and cure ulcer.

Ofloxacin 200 mg, scored film-coated tablet is indicated in the treatment of following bacterial infections. Particular attention should be paid to information available on bacterial resistance to OFLOXACINE before initiating the treatment. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials. In adults - acute pyelonephritis and complicated infections of urinary tract. - Prostatitis of bacterial origin, orchi-epididymitis. - Pelvic inflammatory pathology, in combination with other antibiotics. For the infections mentioned below, ofloxacin should be used only when the antibiotics usually recommended for the treatment of these infections, are deemed inappropriate): - uncomplicated acute cystitis. - Uretrite. - osteoarticular infections. - complicated infections of skin and soft tissue. - Aigue sinusitis of bacterial origin. - Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive broncho-pneumopathy, including chronic bronchitis. - Community pneumonia. Special situations inhalation of anthrax (coal): prophylaxis after exposure and curative treatment during the treatment of infections at pseudomonas aeruginosa and staphylococcus aureus, the emergence of resistant mutants has been described and can justify the association of another antibiotic. Microbiological monitoring in search of such resistance must be considered in particular in the event of suspicion of failure. The use of OFLOXACINE in serious infections, in particular bacteremic at pseudomonas aeruginosa and acinetobacter, is not recommended.

Adults Ofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of bacterial infections with germs sensitive to OFLOXACINE. The mode of administration (intravenous or orally) depends on the indication and severity of the infection: pyelonephritis. Prostatitis, epididymitis, orchitis sepsis due to urogenital infections. Ofloxacin is not indicated in the treatment of syphilis and trichomonases. For the infections mentioned below, OFLOXACINE should only be used when the antibiotics recommended in the initial treatments of these infections are deemed inappropriate: complicated infections of soft and skin. Osteo-articular infections. Acute cystitis, infections of the exacerbation urethra of chronic and recurrent bronchitis caused by the Haemophilus influenzae or other gram negative and multi-resistant germs as well as by the staphylococcus gold. The use of Ofloxacin is indicated in the event of pneumonia due to so -called problems (e.g. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Legionella, Staphylococcus). In the outpatient sector, pneumonia is often due to pneumococci that are not very sensitive to OFLOXACINE. Infections of the small basin (Pelvis) in association with other treatments. Anti-infectious prophylaxis in patients with deficient immune defenses (eg in neutropenic phase). Please consult the official recommendations for the appropriate employment of antibiotics, in particular recommendations to reduce the increase in antibiotic resistance. Children and adolescents The use of OFLOXACINE is not indicated in children and adolescents under the age of 18.

Uses: Ovarian cancer: in first -line ovary cancer chemotherapy, paclitaxel is indicated, in combination with cisplatin, for the treatment of patients with advanced ovarian carcinoma or residual tumor (> 1 cm) after initial laparotomy. In the second -intention chemotherapy of ovarian cancer, paclitaxel is indicated for the treatment of the metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after the failure of standard platinum treatment. Breast cancer: by way of adjuvant treatment, paclitaxel is indicated for the treatment of patients with positive lymph node carcinoma after treatment with anthracycline and cyclophosphamide (AC). Adjuvant treatment with paclitaxel should be envisaged as an alternative to prolonged AC treatment. In monotherapy, paclitaxel is indicated for the treatment of metastatic breast carcinoma in patients who have not responded to standard treatment based on anthracyclines or for which this treatment is contraindicated. Non with advanced bronchial cancer: Paclitaxel, in combination with cisplatin, is indicated for the treatment of bronchial cancer non -small cells (CBNPC) in patients for whom potentially curative surgery and/or radiotherapy is not indicated. Kaposi sarcoma linked to AIDS: Paclitaxel is indicated for the treatment of patients with Kaposi sarcoma (SK) advanced AIDS and which have not responded to previous treatment based on liposomal anthracyclines.

This medication is indicated to reduce high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults. Indapamide is a diuretic. Most diuretics increase the amount of urine produced by the kidneys. However, indapamide is different from other diuretics because it only has a slight increase in the amount of urine produced. In addition, Indapamide dilates blood vessels, which allows blood to circulate more easily. This helps reduce blood pressure.

Pneumovax-23 is indicated for active immunization against infections due to the pneumococcal serotypes contained in the vaccine. The vaccine is recommended for all subjects from the 2nd anniversary with an increased risk of contracting or dying of a pneumococcal infection. Risk groups for which vaccination is recommended are listed in official vaccination recommendations. Pneumococcal infections and serious pneumococcal diseases are a serious danger for the elderly and for patients with chronic conditions. People with chronic cardiovascular diseases (cardiomyopathy), chronic pulmonary diseases (BPCO, emphysema), chronic liver diseases (liver cirrhosis), diabetes mellitus, alcohol or asthma abuse (including chronic bronchitis, emphyseme and long -term administration of systemic corticosteroids) greater risk of contracting with pneumococcus infection and must therefore be vaccinated. Immunodeficent patients (HIV, leukemia, lymphoma, multiple myelome, Hodgkin's disease) and those treated with systemic corticosteroids, after splenectomy or asplénia, including anemia with falciforms and other serious hemoglobinopathies, as well as patients with chronic renal diseases, including nephrotic syndrome, should also be vaccinated. The tolerance and efficiency of the vaccine have not been studied in children under 2 years of age due to the weakness of the immune response in this age group. The vaccine does not protect against acute average otitis, sinusitis or other frequent infections of the upper respiratory tract. Pneumovax-23 should be used in accordance with official vaccine recommendations.

In this case, your doctor can also prescribe antibiotics that make it possible to treat infection and cure ulcer. - Stomach ulcers associated with taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Treatment of premature ejaculation (EP) in adult men aged 18 to 64. Dapoxetine must only be prescribed to patients bringing together all the following criteria: · Time of intravaginal ejaculation (IELT) less than two minutes; and ejaculation which, permanently or recurrently, occurs with minimal sexual stimulation, before, during or shortly after penetration and before the patient wishes; and significant personal suffering or interpersonal difficulties as a consequence of the EP; and · Bad ejaculation control; and history of premature ejaculation in the majority of sex in the last 6 months. Dapoxetine should only be administered as a treatment treatment before planned sexual activity. Dapoxetine should not be prescribed to delay ejaculation in men who have not been diagnosed with an EP. Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Ofloxacin 200 mg, scored film-coated tablet is indicated in the treatment of following bacterial infections. Particular attention should be paid to information available on bacterial resistance to OFLOXACINE before initiating the treatment. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials. In adults - acute pyelonephritis and complicated infections of urinary tract. - Prostatitis of bacterial origin, orchi-epididymitis. - Pelvic inflammatory pathology, in combination with other antibiotics. For the infections mentioned below, ofloxacin should be used only when the antibiotics usually recommended for the treatment of these infections, are deemed inappropriate): - uncomplicated acute cystitis. - Uretrite. - osteoarticular infections. - complicated infections of skin and soft tissue. - Aigue sinusitis of bacterial origin. - Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive broncho-pneumopathy, including chronic bronchitis. - Community pneumonia. Special situations inhalation of anthrax (coal): prophylaxis after exposure and curative treatment during the treatment of infections at pseudomonas aeruginosa and staphylococcus aureus, the emergence of resistant mutants has been described and can justify the association of another antibiotic. Microbiological monitoring in search of such resistance must be considered in particular in the event of suspicion of failure. The use of OFLOXACINE in serious infections, in particular bacteremic at pseudomonas aeruginosa and acinetobacter, is not recommended.

Adults Ofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of bacterial infections with germs sensitive to OFLOXACINE. The mode of administration (intravenous or orally) depends on the indication and severity of the infection: pyelonephritis. Prostatitis, epididymitis, orchitis sepsis due to urogenital infections. Ofloxacin is not indicated in the treatment of syphilis and trichomonases. For the infections mentioned below, OFLOXACINE should only be used when the antibiotics recommended in the initial treatments of these infections are deemed inappropriate: complicated infections of soft and skin. Osteo-articular infections. Acute cystitis, infections of the exacerbation urethra of chronic and recurrent bronchitis caused by the Haemophilus influenzae or other gram negative and multi-resistant germs as well as by the staphylococcus gold. The use of Ofloxacin is indicated in the event of pneumonia due to so -called problems (e.g. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Legionella, Staphylococcus). In the outpatient sector, pneumonia is often due to pneumococci that are not very sensitive to OFLOXACINE. Infections of the small basin (Pelvis) in association with other treatments. Anti-infectious prophylaxis in patients with deficient immune defenses (eg in neutropenic phase). Please consult the official recommendations for the appropriate employment of antibiotics, in particular recommendations to reduce the increase in antibiotic resistance. Children and adolescents The use of OFLOXACINE is not indicated in children and adolescents under the age of 18.

Form: Solution to be diluted for IV infusion
Uses: The active substance contained is the zolédronic acid which belongs to a group of substances called bisphosphonates. Zoledronic acid acts by focusing on the bone and slowing down the bone renewal rate. It is used: - to prevent bone complications, ex. Fractures, in adult patients with bone metastases (dissemination of main site cancer); - to reduce the calcium level in the blood of adult patients when it is high due to the presence of a tumor. Tumors can accelerate the usual bone renewal so that the amount of calcium released by the bone is increased. This pathology is called hypercalcemia induced by tumors.
TherapeuticClass: Drugs for the treatment of bone diseases

Zoledronic acid acts by focusing on the bone and slowing down the bone renewal rate. It is used: - to prevent bone complications, ex. Fractures, in adult patients with bone metastases (dissemination of main site cancer); - to reduce the calcium level in the blood of adult patients when it is high due to the presence of a tumor. Tumors can accelerate the usual bone renewal so that the amount of calcium released by the bone is increased. This pathology is called hypercalcemia induced by tumors.

• schizophrenia. • Olanzapine is indicated in monotherapy, or in treatment associated with lithium or valproate, for the treatment of acute manic episodes of bipolar disorders. Uses: Restorgel® is a colloidal hydroactive gel intended for the treatment of small wounds, which promotes rapid healing of the skin by covering the wound and constituting a wet environment conducive to healing. RESTORGEL® is used after treatment with therapeutic laser and is used to treat superficial burns (also those induced by radiotherapy) and small wounds (for example cutters, cuts). RESTORGEL® can also be used on superficial open wounds. Properties: The Restorgel® colloidal hydroactive formula contributes to quickly soothing the pain caused by small wounds thanks to its refreshing effect. RESTORGEL® contributes to creating optimal healing conditions in order to accelerate cell renewal. Thus, the wound heals faster and the risk of training of scars is reduced. RESTORGEL® forms a protective layer on the wound and protects it against any external contamination. Restorgel® can be used on dry or humid wounds: • In the case of a dry wound, Restorgel® hydrates the wound ("hydrogel" effect). This absorbs the water contained in Restorgel®, which promotes the dissolution of necrotic/lesioned tissue. • In the case of an oozing wound, the hydrocolloid contained in Restorgel® is activated; Restorgel® absorbs excess exsudat and restores and maintains the water balance in the wound ("hydrocolloid" effect).

Uses: They are limited to infections due to the germs defined as sensitive: • Angins documented with beta-hemolytic streptococcus, alternative to beta-lactams treatment, especially when it cannot be used. • Acute sinusitis. Given the microbiological profile of these infections, macrolides are indicated when treatment with a beta-lactamine is impossible. • Surinfections of acute bronchitis. • Exacerbations of chronic bronchitis. • Community pneumopathies in subjects: - without risk factors, - without signs of clinical severity, - in the absence of clinical elements evocative of a pneumococcal etiology. In the event of suspicion of atypical pneumonia, macrolides are indicated regardless of gravity and terrain. • Benign skin infections: impetigo, impetiginization of dermatoses, ecthyma, infectious dermohypodermitis (in particular, erysipelas), erythrasma. • Stomatological infections. • Non -gonococcal genital infections. • Chimioprophylaxis of raa relapses in case of allergy to beta-lactams. • Toxoplasmosis of the pregnant woman. • Prophylaxis of meningococcal meningitis in the event of a contraindication to rifampicin: - The goal is to eradicate the germ (Neisseria meningitidis) of nasopharynx, - spiramycin is not a treatment of meningococcal meningitis, - it is recommended in prophylaxis in: § the patient after her treatment Reintegration into community, § The subjects having been exposed to oropharyngeal secretions within ten days preceding its hospitalization. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials.

Uses: Adults Saxenda is indicated in addition to a hypocaloric diet and an increase in physical activity in weight control in adult patients with an initial body mass (BMI): • ≥ 30 kg/m² (obesity), or • ≥ 27 kg/m² and <30 kg/m² (overweight) in the presence of at least one factor of comorbidity linked to the weight (Type 2 prediabetes or diabetes), high blood pressure, dyslipidemia or obstructive sleep apnea syndrome. Saxenda treatment should be interrupted after 12 weeks at a dose of 3.0 mg/day if patients have not lost at least 5 % of their initial weight. Adolescents (≥ 12 years) Saxenda can be used in addition to a healthy diet and an increase in physical activity in weight control in adolescent patients from 12 years old with: • Obesity (corresponding to a BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² in adults according to international thresholds)* and • body weight greater than 60 kg. Saxenda treatment should be interrupted and reassessed if patients have not lost at least 4 % of their BMI or BMI Z-Score after 12 weeks at a dose of 3.0 mg/day or at the maximum tolerated dose.

Uses: Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Adults Quétiapine is indicated for treatment: - schizophrenia. - Maniac episodes during bipolar disorders, as monotherapy for 12 weeks or in combination of lithium or valproate for 3 to 6 weeks. - depressed episodes during bipolar disorders. Quétiapine is indicated for the prevention of recurrences (with regular control of the risk-risk report) in patients with bipolar disorders who responded satisfactorily to Quetiapine during acute mania episodes or acute depression. In particular to treat depressive episodes during bipolar disorders, the treatment must be initiated and controlled by an experienced doctor in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders. Adolescents (aged 13 to 17) Quétiapine is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia. Children and adolescents (aged 10 to 17) Quétiapine is indicated as a 3 -week monotherapy for acute treatment of mania episodes as part of a bipolar disorder.

In type 2 adult diabetic patients, Sitaglipitine is indicated to improve blood sugar control: in monotherapy · in patients insufficiently controlled by diet and physical exercise alone and for which metformin is contraindicated or is not tolerated. In oral diet, in combination with metformin, when it, used in monotherapy with diet and physical exercise, does not allow adequate control of blood sugar. A hypoglycemic sulfamide, when the latter, used in monotherapy, at the maximum tolerated dose, with diet and physical exercise, does not allow adequate blood sugar control and when metformin is contraindicated or is not tolerated. An agonist of the activating receptors of the proliferation of gamma (pparg) peroxystomes (thiazolidinedione), when it is appropriate and its use in monotherapy with diet and physical exercise, does not allow adequate control of blood sugar. In oral sorthe therapy, in combination with a sulfonamide hypoglycaemant and metformin, when dual therapy with these two drugs with diet and physical exercise does not provide adequate control of blood sugar. A pparg and metformin receptor agonist, when the PPARG receptor agonist is appropriate and a dual therapy with these two drugs with diet and physical exercise does not allow adequate control of blood sugar. Sitagliptine is also indicated in addition to insulin (with or without metformin) when a stable dose of insulin with diet and physical exercise does not allow adequate control of blood sugar.

Rheumatoid arthritis (PR) Simponi, in combination with methotrexate (MTX), is indicated in: • Treatment of active rheumatoid arthritis, moderate to severe in adults, when the response to anti -ulumatic basic treatments (DMARD), including MTX, has been inadequate. • Treatment of active, severe and scalable rheumatoid arthritis in unrealized adults before by the MTX. Simponi has been shown, in combination with MTX, slows down the speed of progression of joint destruction, measured by radiography and improves physical function. Idiopathic juvenile arthritis Juvenile Idiopathic arthritis polyarticular (AJIP) Simponi, in combination with MTX, is indicated in the treatment of arthritis juvenile idiopathic polyarticular in children from 2 years and more, which have not adequately responded to a previous treatment with MTX. Rheumatism psoriasic (RP) Simponi, alone or in combination with the MTX, is indicated in the treatment of active and evolving psoriatism rheumatism in adults, when the response to a previous treatment with DMARD 28 was inadequate. Simponi has been shown that Simponi slows down the speed of progression of peripheral articular destruction, measured by radiography in patients with symmetrical articular forms of the disease and improves physical function. Axial spondyloarthritis Ankylosing spondylitis (SA) Simponi is indicated in the treatment of severe ankylosing spondylitis in adults who have not adequately responded to conventional treatment. Axial non -radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (NR axial spa) Simponi is indicated in the treatment of severe active non -radiographic axial spondyloarthritis of adults with objective signs of inflammation, resulting in a high rate of protein C reactive (CRP) and/or signs visible to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in case of inadequate response or intolerance non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Rectocolite hemorrhagic (RCH) Simponi is indicated in the treatment of active, moderate to severe hemorrhagic rectocolitis, in adult patients who have not adequately responded to conventional treatment including corticosteroids and 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP) or azathioprine (AZA), or in which this treatment is poor tolerated or contraindicated.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials.

Uses: Levofloxacin belongs to a group of drugs called antibiotics. Levofloxacin is an antibiotic of the “Quinolone” type. It acts by killing bacteria responsible for infections in your body. Levofloxacin can be used to treat: - sinus infections. - lungs, in people with chronic respiratory problems or pneumonia. - Urinary tract, especially in terms of your kidneys or your bladder. - Prostate, when you have an infection that lasts. - Subcutaneous skin and fabrics, including muscles. This is sometimes called "soft fabrics". In certain specific situations, levofloxacin can be used to reduce the risk of contracting pulmonary disease called coal disease or the risk of worsening disease after exposure to bacteria responsible for coal disease.
Contraindications: Levofloxacin tablets should not be used: - in hypersensitive patients to levofloxacin or any other quinolone, or to any of the excipients, - in epileptic patients, - in patients with history of tendinopathies linked to the administration of fluoroquinolones, - in children or adolescents in times of growth, - in women who are breastfeeding.

Trazuva should be used only in patients with metastatic gastric cancer whose tumors have an overexpression of HER2 defined by IHC2+ confirmed by a FISH+ or SISH+ result, or by IHC3+. Precise and validated methods of analysis should be used.

Ciprofloxacin is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibiotics. Before the start of processing, it is necessary to take into account in particular the information available relating to resistance, in particular the recommendations of use aimed at avoiding the increase in antibiotic resistance. In the case of uncomplicated infections, ciprofloxacin will only be used when other antibiotics which are usually recommended for the initial treatment of infections in question are considered inappropriate or failed. Adults • Infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by gram negative bacteria o Exacerbations of chronic obstructive bronchopneumopathy (BPCO) o Bronchopulmonary infections in case of cystic fibrosis or bronchitasia o Pneumonia • Chronic purulent otitis • Acute aggravation of chronic sinusitis, in particular when it is caused by gram negative bacteria • Urinary infections • Genital infections provided that strains of neisseria gonorrhoeae resistant to ciprofloxacin could have been excluded. o Uretrite and cervicitis with gonococci o Orchi-epididymitis o Pelvic inflammatory affections (PID) • Infections of the digestive tract (e.g. travel diarrhea) • Intra-abdominal infections • Infections of skin and soft tissues due to gram-negative bacteria • External otitis • Bones and joints • Prevention of invasive infections in Neisseria Meningitidis • Inhalation of coal disease agents (post-exposure and treatment prophylaxis) Ciprofloxacin is suitable for the treatment of neutropenic patients with fever, if it is suspected that fever is caused by bacterial infection. Children and adolescents • Bronchopulmonary infections caused by pseudomonas aeruginosa in patients with cystic fibrosis. • In children from 1 year as a third choice medication in the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections and in the event of pyelonephritis caused by E. coli. The indication of the treatment will only be made in accordance with the specialist, either an infectiologist pediatrician or an infectiologist. In children and adolescents, ciprofloxacin can also be used in case of serious infections if this treatment is deemed necessary. The treatment should only be initiated by an experienced doctor in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and/or serious infections in children and adolescents. Clinical studies on the aforementioned indications have been carried out. For other indications, clinical experience is limited. Children under the age of 6 should be treated with adequate galenic shape, with a suspension or an infusion of ciprofloxacin. Coal (adults and children) for post-exposure prophylaxis and for the treatment of coal after inhalation of the Bacillus anthracis germ. The efficiency of ciprofloxacin in coal has been demonstrated by experiments in animals. In children, adolescents and pregnant women, it is necessary to check whether it is not possible to switch to a treatment by (amino) penicillin when you have the antibiogram of the bacillus anthracis strain involved.

Norfloxacin in the form of tablets is indicated in the treatment of the following infections. Particular attention must be paid to the information available on bacterial resistance to norfloxacin before initiating the treatment. The official recommendations should be taken into account concerning the appropriate use of antibacterials. In adults • Uncomplicated acute cystitis. In uncomplicated acute cystitis, norfloxacin should be used only when antibiotics usually recommended for the treatment of these infections, are deemed inappropriate. • Acute complicated cystitis. • Gonococcal uretricities and cervicites due to a sensitive Neisseria Gonorrhoeae. • Prostatitis of bacterial origin. • Acute uncomplicated acute pyelonephritis. During the treatment of infections at pseudomonas aeruginosa and staphylococcus aureus, the emergence of resistant mutants has been described and can justify the association of another antibiotic. Microbiological monitoring in search of such resistance must be considered in particular in the event of suspicion of failure.

Considerations: Effects on the gastrointestinal tract of ulcers, hemorrhages or perforations of the gastrointestinal tract can occur at any time during treatment with non-stéroid anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), selective inhibitors of COX-2 or not, also without signs of call or anamnestic indices. Some of these complications have had a fatal outcome. Caution will therefore be of rigor in the treatment of patients with a high risk of gastrointestinal complications under NSAIDs: for example elderly patients, people treated simultaneously with other NSAIDs, with inhibitors of platelet aggregation (such as acetylsalicylic acid) or with glucocorticoids or patients drinking alcohol or antecedent Gastrointestinal pathologies such as ulcers or hemorrhages. In order to reduce this risk, the lowest effective dose should always be prescribed for the shortest possible treatment. The simultaneous administration of Cellcoxib and acetylsalicylic acid (even low doses of AAS) increases the risk of gastrointestinal side effects (ulcers and other complications). Long-term clinical studies have not shown significant difference in gastrointestinal tolerance between selective COX-2 + AAS inhibitors and conventional non-stéroid anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) + AAS (see "Properties/Effects-Pharmacodynamics"). Avoid the simultaneous use of Célécoxib and other NSAIDs. Effects on the cardiovascular system of controlled placebo studies have shown an increase in the risk of cardiovascular and cerebroscle thrombotic complications during treatment with certain selective COX-2 inhibitors. It is not yet known whether this risk is directly linked to the COX-1 or COX-2 selectivity of each of the NSAIDs (see under "undesirable effects"). Compared to placebo, an increase in severe cardiovascular accidents, in particular myocardial infarction, has been observed in a long -term study in patients with sporadic adenomatous polyps treated with 2 × 200 mg, respectively 2 × 400 mg of Celeboxib per day. Celebrex should be administered at the lowest effective dose possible and for a shortest duration as possible because the cardiovascular risk may increase with the dose and duration of the treatment. The relative increase in this risk seems to be similar in patients with diseases or cardiovascular risk factors. With regard to the absolute incidence, an increased risk could however exist in patients with diseases or cardiovascular risk factors due to the basic frequency increased for these patients. The need for treatment as well as the response to it should be regularly reassessed, especially in patients with osteoarthrosis (see under "contraindications", "adverse effects" and "properties/effects-pharmacodynamics"). Patients with a considerable risk of cardiovascular problems (eg hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, smoking) or with an obliterating peripheral arteriopathy should only be treated by celebrity of celebration after a careful risk and profits assessment. (See under "Effects on kidneys, hypertension" and "Properties/Effects"). Selective COX-2 inhibitors cannot replace acetylsalicylic acid for the prevention of thromboembolic cardiovascular diseases because they have no effect on thrombocytes. Consequently, anticoagulant treatment should not be interrupted (see under "properties/effects"). Effects on kidneys, hypertension in clinical studies, kidney effects similar to those encountered under comparative NSAIDs have been observed under Cellcoxib. Water retention with edema and/or high blood pressure and nephrotoxicity are part of the renal effects of NSAIDs. Water retention/edema: In patients with reduced cardiac function and predisposition to water retention, Celebrex should be used with caution, as the inhibition of prostaglandins synthesis can deny the kidney function and cause greater liquid retention. Caution is also required in people who simultaneously take diuretics or IEC inhibitors as well as in the event of increased risk of hypovolemia. Hypertension: Like all NSAIDs, celebration can also cause the occurrence or worsening of existing hypertension. Both can help increase the frequency of cardiovascular events (see "effects on the cardiovascular system"). NSAIDs, including Celeboxib, should therefore be used with caution in hypertensive patients. Blood pressure should be closely monitored at the start and during the treatment with Celeboxib (see "Properties/Effects - Pharmacodynamics"). Nephrotoxicity: NSAIDs, including celebration, can be nephrotoxic. The risk of nephrotoxicity is maximum in patients with alteration of kidney function, heart failure or liver conditions as well as in elderly patients. These patients should be closely monitored during treatment with Celeboxib. Anaphylactoid reactions and skin reactions of very rare severe skin reactions, including exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, were reported in relation to the taking of Cellcoxib, some with a deadly outcome (see under "undesirable effects"). It is at the start of treatment that the risk seems to be the highest, most of the reported reactions having occurred during the first month of treatment. Severe hypersensitivity reactions (anaphylaxis and angioedema) have been reported in patients who had taken celebration (see "undesirable effects"). Patients with an allergy known to sulfonamides or other drugs may present an increased risk of developing severe skin reactions or hypersensitivity reactions (see under "contraindications"). Treatment should be interrupted at the slightest sign of rash, mucous membranes or signs evoking hypersensitivity. Effects on the liver A few cases of severe hepatic reactions have been described under treatment by Celeboxib. These, among other things, include fulminant hepatitis (in certain cases of fatal outcome), liver necrosis and liver failure (in certain cases of fatal outcome or having required hepatic transplantation). In cases where it was possible to document the time of the occurrence of reactions, most of the severe liver side hepatic effects developed in the month following the start of treatment with Celeboxib (see "adverse effects"). Increases and complementary precautions The elderly patients more often have a reduced renal or hepatic function as well as a cardiac dysfunction. For these reasons, elderly patients should be followed more attention by their doctor. If during the treatment there was a pejoration of the function of the organs described above, you must think of taking the necessary measures and of interrupting the treatment of Celloxib. Celeboxib inhibits cytochrome oxidase CYP2D6. Even if inhibition is not very marked, it may be necessary to reduce the doses of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6 and whose dose is appropriate individually (see "Interactions"). Patients known to be slow metabolizers of CYP2C9 should be treated with caution (see under "pharmacokinetics"). Celeboxib can hide fever and other signs of inflammation. The concomitant use of NSAIDs and oral anticoagulants increases the risk of hemorrhage and must be done with caution. Oral anticoagulants include coumarin type warfarin and new oral anticoagulants (eg apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban). In patients treated jointly with warfarin or similar active substances, some have been observed severe hemorrhages, some of which have been fatal. Due to the increase in thromboplastin time (INR) reported, coagulation/INR should be monitored in patients with coumarin type warfarin, at the start of treatment or after a modification of the celebrity dose (see under "interactions"). Celebrex 100 mg and 200 mg capsules contain lactose (142.2 mg respectively 47.3 mg, calculated in the form of anhydrous substance). This medication should not be used by people with rare metabolic disease such as galactose intolerance, lapp-lactase deficit or glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome. Systemic idiopathic idiopathic arthritis, including Cellcoxib, should be used with caution in the systemic form of AJI because of the risk of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Patients with systemic AIJ, receiving celebration, should be monitored in order to detect any development of coagulation test anomalies.

Moxifloxacin 400 mg film-coated tablet is indicated in patients aged 18 and over to treat the following bacterial infections when due to bacteria towards which moxifloxacin is active. It should be used to treat these infections only when the usual antibiotics are not appropriate or when they have not been effective: - acute sinus infections (acute bacterial sinusitis), - sudden aggravations of chronic inflammation of the respiratory tract (acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis), infections of lungs (pneumonia) The hospital, with the exception of severe cases, - mild to moderate to moderate to women (pelvic infections), including trumpet infections and uterine mucosa infections. Treating only these infections of the woman's high genital system by Moxifloxacin is not enough; Therefore, for this type of infections, the doctor prescribes another antibiotic, in combination with moxifloxacin. Moxifloxacin 400 mg film-coated tablet can also be prescribed in relay of the intravenous form when the following bacterial infections showed a favorable evolution: - skin and soft tissue infections, - lung infections (pneumonia) contracted outside the hospital. Moxifloxacin 400 mg film-coated tablet should not be used to initiate treatment in skin and soft tissue infections or in severe lung infections.

Data in hospitalized patients with serious depression and high risk of suicide are insufficient. In the presence of obsessive compulsive disorders that initially responded to treatment, lasting efficiency, safety and tolerance has been noted during seraline treatment of a duration of up to two years. Panic disorders Seraline is indicated for the treatment of panic attacks, with or without agoraphobia. Post-traumatic stress, seraline is indicated to alleviate the symptoms of the chronic state of post-traumatic stress. Social phobia SERTALINE is indicated for the treatment of social phobia. Long -term efficiency (over 24 weeks) for the treatment of social phobia has not yet been established.

The active substance contained is the zolédronic acid which belongs to a group of substances called bisphosphonates. Zoledronic acid acts by focusing on the bone and slowing down the bone renewal rate. It is used: - to prevent bone complications, ex. Fractures, in adult patients with bone metastases (dissemination of main site cancer); - to reduce the calcium level in the blood of adult patients when it is high due to the presence of a tumor. Tumors can accelerate the usual bone renewal so that the amount of calcium released by the bone is increased. This pathology is called hypercalcemia induced by tumors.
TherapeuticClass: Drugs for the treatment of bone diseases

Uses: Treatment of adult patients suffering from the following infections: - Nosocomial pneumonia, provided that it is proven or very likely that it is caused by stumps of staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pneumoniae sensitive to linezolid. Experience in infections caused by pneumococci resistant to penicillin is limited. The linezolid is not effective in the event of Gram -negative infections. If a mixed infection due to gram negative germs is suspected or attested, a specific treatment must be established simultaneously against gram negative germs. To date, only Aztréonam and the Aminosides have been tested. - Complicated infections of the skin and soft tissues: with regard to the treatment of complicated infections of the skin and soft tissues, Zyvoxid is indicated only when established, after determination of microbiological sensitivity, that infection is caused by sensitive gram -gram bacteria belonging to staphylococcus aureus, stuptococcus pyogenic or Agalactiae. The linezolid is not effective in the event of Gram -negative infections. In patients suffering from complicated infections of the skin and soft tissues, in whom a co-infection due to gram negative germs is presumed or attested, the linezolid should be used only if there is no other possible treatment (see the section "Warnings and precautions"). In such cases, you must simultaneously establish a treatment for gram negative germs. To date, only Aztréonam and the Aminosides have been tested. There is no experience in the treatment of diabetic ulcers or decubitus. - Enterococcus faecium infections resistant to vancomycin, including bacteremia. There is no experience in the treatment of SNC infections, osteomyelitis and endocarditis.
